newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Smith Barney wins Fla. deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Smith Barney wins Fla. deal.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary prices remained largely static at midday Tuesday, while primary market action saw Smith Barney Inc win $300 million Florida environmental bonds.

"I don't think the bid is really up, futures are up a little bit, but the cash market is just kind of unchanged and directionless," a municipal trader said. "We don't really have anything important economically until Thursday when we get jobless claims, if you call that important, and then home sales on Friday."
As for customer selling, the trader said lists were not overwhelming with less than $200 million out for the bid.
A second trader also described secondary market action as quiet.
"The market is not doing an awful lot, it just seems to be kind of struggling along," he said.

Tuesday's actively quoted issues included Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey 5-1/2 percent bonds of January 2026. The bonds had a 5.86 percent net bid Tuesday, versus Monday's closing net bid of 5.83 percent.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 6/32 at 94-14/32 to yield 7.07 percent.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract was up 8/32 at 112-27/32. The June T-bond contract was up 7/32 at 107-28/32. The MOB spread was 159 ticks.

Turning to new issues, Smith Barney won $300 million Florida Department of Environmental Protection Preservation 2000 revenue bonds at a true interest cost of 5.37 percent. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.4 percent in 2013.

In negotiated action, Smith Barney Inc. repriced $150 million King County, Wash., general obligation bonds, cutting yields in several maturities. The top yield was lowered to 5.75 from 5.80 percent in 2011.

Also Tuesday, J.P. Morgan Securities began a one-day retail order period for a $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corporation deal. The firm offered the 2005 maturity at a 5.25 percent yield.
Goldman Sachs & Co Wednesday is expected to price a $500 million Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees offering.
